verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Ψ = r⁻¹I_c(rγ_d) is literally the body of PressureStream.streamPotential (divideRadius ∘ physicalCompact ∘ weightedSource), and I_c g = I g − χ_m J g is literally the body of TransportPrimitive.compactIntegral, with I = pastIntegral and J = totalIntegral. Two encoding differences. (a) Limits: Lean's I integrates over u ∈ (−∞,0] and J over all of ℝ along the transport line z + (u,(Mu)•v), where the paper writes ∫_0^r and ∫_0^∞ in r; physicalCompact_eq_radialIntegral converts these to ∫_a^r and ∫_a^b in the physical radius, which equals the paper's 0..r and 0..∞ because g is shell-supported in [a,b] with smooth zero extension. (b) Lean states one operator carrying the transport speed M and the power coordinate U = R^d, so the paper's phase shift ((r')^{d_r} − r^{d_r})v_r of (8.4) is the case M = 1 of Lean's M(s^d − r^d)•v and the normalized (8.5) is M = Λ_{i g0}Q^{d_r}/2; χ_m is TransportPrimitive.interiorCutoff (a^d) (b^d) evaluated at r^d, matching the paper's slow cutoff that is zero on the inner collar and one on the outer collar of the active shell.
